transcripts.transcript:
Private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here, returning your portfolio-review call. Office quite busy today, but I've stepped away from the desk. Easier to speak now lah, rather than keep missing each other.

Thank you for returning my call, Adrian. Before we discuss the review, may I have your identification details and date of birth?

Got a quiet room now, so you should hear me clearly. My FIN is G six six eight three nine zero nine L. My date of birth is the twenty-eighth of November nineteen seventy-four.

Your objective is long-term capital growth through diversified global equities, using money you do not need for near-term business or personal expenses. That is the objective I am working with. To start with, there is Summit Global Equity ETF, which provides diversified exposure to global equities through a pooled portfolio. For comparison, there is also Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, a corporate debt security whose payments depend on the issuer meeting its obligations.

I'll take the one you mentioned first, the global equity fund. For this transaction, use American dollars ah.

I recommend this fund because it gives you diversified global equity exposure for your long-term growth goal, without requiring you to select and monitor individual companies. Even though this fund holds a diversified portfolio, a broad fall in global equity markets can still reduce its market value. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest. Are you willing to bear investment losses in pursuing your long-term growth objective?

Yes, I am willing to take investment losses for long-term growth. Substantial declines also I can accept. For the rest of our conversation, keep the explanations short ah. At work got people coming to the door, even when the calendar says I'm unavailable.

I'll keep the remaining points concise. For future contact, would you prefer a message before I telephone, so you can choose a convenient moment?

Message first would help. Sometimes I'm with suppliers, cannot pick up straight away. Telephone still easier than a long email chain lah, especially when I'm moving between appointments.

I can note that contact preference. You had also mentioned enjoying travel. Is your schedule mostly business travel at present, or have you been able to take a break?

Mostly work these days lor. I try to leave some free time when I travel, otherwise only see meeting rooms and airport lounges. My wife says that one doesn't count as a holiday.

A proper break would certainly be different from a work itinerary. When you're away, is the secure message channel still convenient, or would you rather leave routine correspondence until you return?

Secure messages can. Got access on my phone, and I usually check while waiting at the airport. I read business news then also, but by boarding time my attention gone already.

I'll use that channel for routine correspondence and send a message before calling. Returning to the transaction, there is also the fee disclosure. The transaction fee is 0.2% of the transaction amount.

Let me finish the details before someone comes looking for me ah. The amount I'm putting into this transaction is 250,000. For the quantity, put down 700 units. I want to buy, not sell. Make it a limit order, with the limit price at 357.14 US dollars.

For the associated correspondence, would you prefer to view the documents in your secure inbox rather than arrange a paper copy?

Secure inbox is fine. Paper copy no need lah, my desk already full of supplier catalogues. If I need to find something later, much easier to search on screen.

I'll note the electronic correspondence preference. If you have an administrative question when you look at the documents, you can contact me through the secure channel.

Thanks Rachel. For calls, just message first as we discussed. No need to chase if I don't answer straight away; usually stuck in a meeting, not ignoring you.

Certainly, Adrian. Thank you for calling back and for setting aside the time. I'll let you return to your work.

Thanks, you too. Better get back before they come searching for me again lah. Bye.
